reasons: The cited text (§ 12.4) is a one-way, 24-month prohibition on Customer soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee 'regardless of how the employee applies' — a no-hire covering all Vendor personnel with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out, correctly classified as a deviation at the walk-away edge.

Deleting the paragraph implements the playbook's preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer') and satisfies the redline guidance to 'delete any no-hire'; the fallback (mutual, 12 months, personnel directly involved, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) is offered in the comment rather than lost.
Failed deterministic checks for duration and carve-out are artifacts of full deletion, not defects — no residual restrictive language remains that could require a 12-month cap or carve-out sentence.

Comment is concise, first-person plural, prefixed, states what changed and why, and cites the playbook position; the § 12.3 inconsistency argument is a useful negotiation hook, though it rests on text outside the supplied paragraphs and should be spot-checked before sending.
